question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:

Assertion (A): The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar to commemorate his conquest of Gujarat.

Reason (R): Fatehpur Sikri was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. The Buland Darwaza ("Gate of Victory"), built in 1576, was raised by Akbar to commemorate his victory over Gujarat. At about 54 metres, it is one of the tallest gateways in the world and forms the southern entrance to the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri. (बुलंद दरवाज़ा — फ़तेहपुर सीकरी)

 

• Reason (R) is true. Fatehpur Sikri was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

 

• However, R is not the explanation of A. The gateway was built to mark a military conquest in the sixteenth century; its listing by UNESCO four centuries later is an entirely separate fact and cannot explain why Akbar built it.

 

• Fatehpur Sikri, built largely in red sandstone, was founded by Akbar in 1571 in honour of the Sufi saint Shaikh Salim Chishti, and served as the Mughal capital for roughly 14 years before being abandoned, chiefly because of a scarcity of water. Its notable structures include the Diwan-i-Khas, Panch Mahal, Jodha Bai's Palace, Ibadat Khana and the Tomb of Salim Chishti.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Humayun's Tomb in Delhi (built by Hamida Banu Begum, 1570) was the first major Mughal garden tomb and introduced the charbagh layout and the double dome, features later perfected in the Taj Mahal.

 

• Other Mughal UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India: the Taj Mahal (1983), Agra Fort (1983), Humayun's Tomb (1993) and the Red Fort Complex (2007).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Both statements are true, but there is no causal link between them.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.

question: In the Mauryan administration, the officials known as 'Rajukas' were chiefly concerned with which of the following?
option_2: Collection of customs duties at ports
option_3: Land survey, revenue assessment and, later, justice in the rural areas
option_4: Supervision of the royal mint and treasury
solution_text:
The correct answer is Land survey, revenue assessment and, later, justice in the rural areas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajukas were Mauryan officers placed in charge of rural administration. Their original duty was the survey and assessment of land for revenue, and Ashoka, in his Pillar Edict IV, extended their powers to include the award of punishment and the dispensing of justice, granting them independence in these matters. (राजुक — मौर्य ग्रामीण प्रशासन)

 

• The Mauryan Empire had a highly centralised administration with the king at the apex, assisted by a Mantriparishad (council of ministers) and a large bureaucracy of Adhyakshas (superintendents) described in Kautilya's Arthashastra.

 

• Other important Mauryan officials:

◦ Samaharta — the highest officer in charge of revenue collection

◦ Sannidhata — the chief treasurer, in charge of the state store-house

◦ Yuktas — subordinate officers handling the king's revenue and accounts

◦ Pradeshika — the head of a district, who supervised the Rajukas

◦ Dhamma Mahamatta — a special class of officers created by Ashoka to propagate *dhamma*

◦ Sitadhyaksha — superintendent of agriculture; Panyadhyaksha — of commerce; Akaradhyaksha — of mines

 

• The empire was divided into provinces, four of which are known from the edicts — Taxila (Uttarapatha), Ujjain (Avantiratha), Suvarnagiri (Dakshinapatha) and Tosali (Kalinga) — each usually under a prince (Kumara).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador of Seleucus Nicator at the court of Chandragupta Maurya, wrote the Indica, which describes the administration of Pataliputra by a municipal body of 30 members divided into 6 committees of 5.

 

• The Mauryan dynasty was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya), and the last ruler, Brihadratha, was killed by his commander Pushyamitra Shunga in about 185 BCE.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Military affairs were managed by a war office of 30 members in 6 boards, as described by Megasthenes.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Customs and tolls were the concern of the Shulkadhyaksha.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The treasury was under the Sannidhata, and the mint under the Lakshanadhyaksha.

question: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of Carnatic Music' (Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Purandara Dasa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Purandara Dasa (1484-1564) is honoured as the "Pitamaha" (father or grandsire) of Carnatic music. (पुरंदर दास — कर्नाटक संगीत के पितामह)

 

• He systematised the teaching of Carnatic music, introducing the graded exercises still used today — the sarali varise, janti varise, alankaras and the geetams — and he adopted Mayamalavagowla as the basic raga for beginners.

 

• He belonged to the Haridasa devotional movement of Karnataka and composed thousands of devaranamas in Kannada, signing them with the pen-name (*ankita*) "Purandara Vittala".

 

• The Trinity of Carnatic music — Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri — all lived in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries at Tiruvarur in Tamil Nadu, well after Purandara Dasa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 72 Melakarta scheme of parent ragas was formulated by Venkatamakhi in his work Chaturdandi Prakashika (17th century); ragas are held to have evolved from the older jatis.

 

• Carnatic music's principal forms are the varnam, kriti, ragam-tanam-pallavi and tillana; its chief accompanying instruments are the mridangam, violin, ghatam and kanjira.

 

• The Tyagaraja Aradhana at Thiruvaiyaru and the Madras Music Season in Chennai are the best-known Carnatic music festivals.

 

NOTE

 

• Tyagaraja (Option 1): One of the Trinity, composer of the Pancharatna Kritis, mostly in Telugu.

 

• Venkatamakhi (Option 2): Formulated the 72 Melakarta raga system, but is not called the father of Carnatic music.

 

• Swathi Thirunal (Option 3): The nineteenth-century ruler of Travancore and a prolific composer in both the Carnatic and Hindustani traditions.

question:
Consider the following statements about athletics events:

1) In the high jump, the technique in which the athlete crosses the bar head first and back downwards is called the Fosbury Flop.

2) In a relay race, the baton must be exchanged within a marked take-over zone.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Fosbury Flop is the high-jump technique in which the athlete approaches on a curve and clears the bar head first, with the back to the bar and facing upwards. It is named after the American jumper Dick Fosbury, who used it to win gold at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics, after which it replaced the older straddle and scissors techniques. (फ़ॉस्बरी फ़्लॉप — ऊँची कूद)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. In relay races the baton must be passed within a marked take-over (exchange) zone, which is 30 metres long under current World Athletics rules. Passing outside the zone leads to disqualification, and the baton, if dropped, must be recovered by the athlete who dropped it.

 

• The standard relay events at the Olympics are the 4 x 100 m and the 4 x 400 m, along with the 4 x 400 m mixed relay.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Some standard athletics measurements: the shot put circle is 2.135 m in diameter and the discus circle 2.50 m; a standard outdoor track is 400 m with 8 lanes; a marathon is 42.195 km.

 

• The world governing body for athletics is World Athletics (formerly the IAAF), founded in 1912 and headquartered at Monaco. Neeraj Chopra won India's first Olympic athletics gold in the javelin throw at Tokyo 2020.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both the statements given are factually accurate.

question: At which edition of the Olympic Games did Vijender Singh win a bronze medal, India's first ever Olympic medal in boxing?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beijing 2008.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vijender Singh won a bronze medal in the middleweight (75 kg) category at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, becoming the first Indian boxer ever to win an Olympic medal. (विजेंदर सिंह — 2008 बीजिंग ओलंपिक, कांस्य पदक)

 

• He hails from Bhiwani in Haryana, a town often called the "Little Cuba" of India for the number of boxers it has produced. He was awarded the Arjuna Award (2010), the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2009) and the Padma Shri (2010), and turned professional in 2015.

 

• At the same Beijing Games, Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold in the 10 m air rifle, and Sushil Kumar won a bronze in wrestling — India's best Olympic performance until then.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other Olympic boxing medals have both been won by women: Mary Kom (bronze, flyweight, London 2012) and Lovlina Borgohain (bronze, welterweight, Tokyo 2020).

 

• MC Mary Kom is a six-time World Amateur Boxing champion and was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2020.

 

• The international governing body for the sport is World Boxing; boxing has featured at the Olympics since 1904.

 

NOTE

 

• Athens 2004 (Option 1): India's only medal was Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore's silver in double trap shooting.

 

• London 2012 (Option 3): India won six medals, including Mary Kom's boxing bronze — but that was after Vijender Singh's.

 

• Rio de Janeiro 2016 (Option 4): India won two medals — P.V. Sindhu (silver, badminton) and Sakshi Malik (bronze, wrestling).

question: Which of the following changes was introduced in the administration of the East India Company by Pitt's India Act of 1784?
option_1: It established a Board of Control to supervise the civil, military and revenue affairs of the Company.
option_2: It ended the Company's monopoly of trade with India.
option_3: It created for the first time the office of the Governor-General of Bengal.
option_4: It transferred the Indian possessions of the Company to the British Crown.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It established a Board of Control to supervise the civil, military and revenue affairs of the Company.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pitt's India Act of 1784, passed during the ministry of William Pitt the Younger, created a Board of Control to superintend the civil, military and revenue affairs of the East India Company in India. (पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट, 1784)

 

• The Act introduced a system of double government: the Court of Directors continued to manage the Company's commercial affairs, while the Board of Control handled its political affairs. This made the Company's Indian territories, for the first time, formally subject to British Government control.

 

• The Act also, for the first time, described the Company's Indian territories as the "British possessions in India".

 

• Its predecessor, the Regulating Act of 1773, was the first step of parliamentary control: it designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings being the first), set up a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774), and reformed the Company's constitution at home as well as its territorial administration in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Landmarks in the constitutional development of British India:

◦ Charter Act 1813 — ended the Company's trade monopoly in India (except tea and trade with China)

◦ Charter Act 1833 — made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (William Bentinck being the first) and ended the Company's commercial functions altogether

◦ Charter Act 1853 — introduced open competition for the civil services

◦ Government of India Act 1858 — abolished the Company and transferred power to the British Crown, creating the post of Secretary of State for India

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The Company's trade monopoly in India was ended by the Charter Act of 1813.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The office of Governor-General of Bengal was created by the Regulating Act of 1773.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The transfer of the Company's territories to the Crown took place under the Government of India Act, 1858, after the Revolt of 1857.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indus Waters Treaty:

1) The Treaty, signed in 1960, allots the waters of the eastern rivers - the Ravi, the Beas and the Sutlej - to India.

2) The World Bank was a signatory to the Treaty and has a specified role in resolving disputes under it.

Which of the statements above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2 are Correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Indus Waters Treaty was signed at Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Jawaharlal Nehru and General Ayub Khan. It allots the three eastern rivers — the Ravi, the Beas and the Sutlej — to India, and the three western rivers — the Indus, the Jhelum and the Chenab — to Pakistan, with India permitted limited non-consumptive, agricultural and run-of-the-river hydroelectric use of the western rivers. (सिंधु जल संधि, 1960)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. The Treaty was brokered by the World Bank, which signed it as a third party. The Bank has a defined procedural role: it appoints a Neutral Expert for "differences" and helps constitute a Court of Arbitration for "disputes".

 

• The Treaty also set up a Permanent Indus Commission, with a commissioner from each country, which is required to meet at least once a year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other important water-sharing arrangements with its neighbours:

◦ The Ganga Water Treaty (1996) with Bangladesh, on sharing the flow at the Farakka Barrage, which applies during the lean season from 1 January to 31 May, not throughout the year

◦ The Mahakali Treaty (1996) with Nepal, covering the Sarada Barrage, Tanakpur Barrage and the Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project

◦ The Kosi (1954) and Gandak (1959) agreements with Nepal

 

• The Indus rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and enters India in Ladakh; the Sutlej rises from the Rakas Lake.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect, because both the given statements are factually accurate.

question:
Fill in the blank:

The first edition of the Khelo India School Games, under the Khelo India programme of the Government of India, was held in the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2018.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Khelo India School Games were held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, New Delhi, in January 2018. Haryana topped the medal tally in that inaugural edition. (खेलो इंडिया — 2018 में पहला संस्करण)

 

• The Khelo India scheme was launched by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to revive the sports culture in India at the grassroots level by building a strong framework for all sports and establishing India as a great sporting nation.

 

• From 2019 the event was renamed the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG), and the programme has since expanded into the Khelo India University Games, the Khelo India Winter Games and the Khelo India Para Games.

 

• Selected athletes receive an annual scholarship for eight consecutive years, and the scheme also funds the creation of Khelo India Centres and Khelo India Accredited Academies across the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS), launched in 2014, supports elite athletes with a realistic chance of an Olympic medal, and is the complement to Khelo India's grassroots focus.

 

• India's highest sporting honour is the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (renamed in 2021 from the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna); the Arjuna Award recognises consistent outstanding performance, and the Dronacharya Award honours coaches.

 

• National Sports Day is observed on 29 August, the birth anniversary of the hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.

 

NOTE

 

• 2014 (Option 1): The year the Target Olympic Podium Scheme was introduced.

 

• 2016 (Option 2) and 2020 (Option 4) are incorrect; the inaugural Khelo India School Games were held in January 2018.

question:
Consider the following statements about "Gitanjali":

1) It is a collection of devotional poems written by Rabindranath Tagore.

2) Its English translation won Tagore the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.

3) The introduction to the English edition was written by W.B. Yeats.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements are correct. "Gitanjali" (Song Offerings) is a collection of devotional poems by Rabindranath Tagore, first published in Bengali in 1910. (गीतांजलि — रवीन्द्रनाथ टैगोर)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Tagore's own English rendering, published in 1912, won him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, making him the first Asian and the first non-European to receive a Nobel Prize.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: The introduction to the English edition was written by the Irish poet W.B. Yeats, who was instrumental in bringing Tagore's work to the notice of Western readers.

 

• Tagore was knighted in 1915 and renounced the knighthood in 1919 in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. He composed "Jana Gana Mana", the national anthem of India, and "Amar Sonar Bangla", the national anthem of Bangladesh; "Namo Namo Matha", the Sri Lankan anthem, was also inspired by him.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major works of Tagore include Gora, Ghare Baire (The Home and the World), Chokher Bali, Kabuliwala, Shesher Kabita and the play Dak Ghar (The Post Office). He founded Visva-Bharati at Santiniketan in 1921.

 

• Indian and India-born Nobel laureates in other fields include C.V. Raman (Physics, 1930), Mother Teresa (Peace, 1979), Amartya Sen (Economics, 1998), Kailash Satyarthi (Peace, 2014) and Abhijit Banerjee (Economics, 2019).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect because each of them omits at least one statement that is factually accurate.

question: Who was sworn in as the 15th Vice-President of India in September 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C.P. Radhakrishnan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• C.P. Radhakrishnan was sworn in as the 15th Vice-President of India on 12 September 2025, the oath being administered by President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan. (सी. पी. राधाकृष्णन — भारत के 15वें उपराष्ट्रपति)

 

• He won the election held on 9 September 2025, securing 452 votes against 300 polled by the opposition candidate, former Supreme Court judge B. Sudershan Reddy. The election was necessitated by the resignation of Jagdeep Dhankhar in July 2025.

 

• Before this he had served as the Governor of Jharkhand and the Governor of Maharashtra.

 

• The Vice-President is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64). He is elected under Article 66 by an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated members, by a system of proportional representation with a single transferable vote, through a secret ballot. The term of office is five years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Unlike the Presidential election, the State Legislative Assemblies take no part in the election of the Vice-President.

 

• To qualify, a person must be a citizen of India, have completed 35 years of age, and be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha.

 

• Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the first Vice-President of India; the Vice-President may be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

 

NOTE

 

• Jagdeep Dhankhar (Option 1): The 14th Vice-President, who resigned in July 2025 before completing his term.

 

• B. Sudershan Reddy (Option 3): A former judge of the Supreme Court and the opposition's candidate in the 2025 election.

 

• Om Birla (Option 4): The Speaker of the Lok Sabha, an entirely different constitutional office.

question: Which of the following is the most rapid form of mass movement, in which rock fragments fall freely down a very steep or vertical slope?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rockfall.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rockfall is the fastest type of mass movement. Blocks of rock become detached from a steep cliff or vertical face and fall freely under gravity, collecting at the base as a talus or scree slope. (शैल पतन — सबसे तीव्र वृहत् संचलन)

 

• Mass movement (mass wasting) is the downslope movement of rock and soil under the direct influence of gravity, without a transporting agent such as running water, wind or ice. Its main triggers are slope steepness, water saturation, earthquakes, deforestation and undercutting of slopes.

 

• Types of mass movement, from slowest to fastest:

◦ Soil creep — extremely slow, imperceptible downhill movement of soil, revealed by tilted poles and bent tree trunks

◦ Solifluction — slow flow of water-saturated soil over frozen sub-soil, typical of periglacial regions

◦ Earthflow and mudflow — moderately rapid flow of saturated material

◦ Slump (slumping) — sliding of a mass along a curved (concave) surface, with a characteristic backward rotation of the slipping block

◦ Landslide, debris fall and rockfall — rapid to very rapid

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• In India, landslides are most frequent in the Himalayas and the Western Ghats, and the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), set up under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, issues guidelines for their management.

 

• The Geological Survey of India (GSI), established in 1851 and headquartered at Kolkata, is the nodal agency for landslide studies and hazard zonation mapping in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Soil creep (Option 1): The slowest of all mass movements, measured in millimetres a year.

 

• Solifluction (Option 2): A slow flow of saturated debris, characteristic of cold, periglacial environments.

 

• Slump (Option 3): Involves a backward rotation of the slipping material along a curved plane; it is comparatively rapid, but the material slides rather than falls freely.

question: In the Indian Census, the sex ratio is defined as which of the following?
option_1: The number of females per 1,000 males
option_2: The number of males per 1,000 females
option_3: The number of females per 100 males
option_4: The ratio of male births to female births in a year
solution_text:
The correct answer is The number of females per 1,000 males.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In India, the sex ratio is defined as the number of females per 1,000 males in the population. (लिंगानुपात — प्रति 1,000 पुरुषों पर महिलाओं की संख्या)

 

• According to Census 2011, India's sex ratio was 943 females per 1,000 males, an improvement over 933 in 2001. The child sex ratio (0-6 years) was 919, the lowest recorded since Independence.

 

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio (1,084) among the states and Haryana the lowest (879). Among union territories, Puducherry was highest (1,037) and Daman and Diu lowest (618).

 

• Note that many other countries, and the United Nations, define the sex ratio the other way round — as the number of males per 100 or 1,000 females — so the Indian usage must be remembered.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other key Census 2011 figures: population 121.09 crore; density 382 persons per sq km; literacy rate 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%); decadal growth 17.7%; Uttar Pradesh the most populous state and Sikkim the least; Bihar the most densely populated state and Arunachal Pradesh the least.

 

• Population density is the number of persons per square kilometre, and is calculated as the total population divided by the total land area.

 

• The Census of India is conducted every ten years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs; the first synchronous census was held in 1881.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: This is the definition used in several other countries and by the UN, but not the one used in the Indian Census.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The Indian sex ratio is expressed per 1,000 males, not per 100.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The ratio of male to female births in a year is the sex ratio at birth, a distinct measure.

question:
Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): India is currently passing through a phase of demographic dividend.

Reason (R): A large proportion of India's population falls in the working-age group of 15 to 59 years.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. India is passing through a phase of demographic dividend — the period in which the growth potential of the economy rises because the share of the working-age population exceeds that of the dependent population. (जनसांख्यिकीय लाभांश)

 

• Reason (R) is true. A large share of India's population lies in the working-age group of 15 to 59 years, and India is among the youngest large populations in the world, with a median age of about 28 years.

 

• R correctly explains A. The demographic dividend arises precisely because the working-age share is large and the dependency ratio — the ratio of the population aged below 15 and above 59 to the working-age population — is low. A larger workforce relative to dependents means higher savings, higher output and faster growth, provided that the workforce is healthy, educated and productively employed.

 

• The dividend is a window of opportunity, not a guarantee: without adequate investment in education, skills and job creation it can turn into a demographic burden through unemployment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The demographic transition theory describes the movement of a society from high birth and high death rates (Stage 1), through falling death rates with high birth rates and rapid population growth (Stage 2, the phase of population explosion), to low birth and low death rates (Stage 3). India is broadly in the later part of the second and the third stage.

 

• Total Fertility Rate (TFR), the average number of children a woman bears in her lifetime, has fallen to about 2.0 in India as per NFHS-5 (2019-21) — below the replacement level of 2.1.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: R is not merely an additional true fact; it is the very reason for the demographic dividend.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.

question: Which of the following best describes the fundamental objective of 'digital twin' technology in industrial systems?
option_1: To create a real-time virtual replica of a physical asset for monitoring, simulation and predictive maintenance
option_2: To encrypt industrial control data on a distributed blockchain ledger
option_3: To duplicate a company's servers at a remote site for disaster recovery
option_4: To replace physical prototypes with 3D-printed models for product marketing
solution_text:
The correct answer is To create a real-time virtual replica of a physical asset for monitoring, simulation and predictive maintenance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A digital twin is a dynamic virtual model of a physical object, process or system, continuously updated with real-time data streamed from sensors on the physical asset. (डिजिटल ट्विन — भौतिक वस्तु की आभासी प्रतिकृति)

 

• Its fundamental purpose is to allow engineers to monitor performance, run simulations and "what-if" scenarios, and predict failures before they occur, so that maintenance can be scheduled in advance. This is called predictive maintenance, and it reduces downtime and cost.

 

• The concept relies on the Internet of Things (IoT) for data capture, cloud computing for storage, and artificial intelligence and machine learning for analysis. It is widely used in aerospace, manufacturing, power generation, urban planning and healthcare.

 

• A digital twin differs from an ordinary simulation in that it is linked in real time to a specific, existing physical counterpart, whereas a simulation usually models a class of objects offline.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related emerging technologies:

◦ Generative design — software that uses algorithms to generate many design options meeting given constraints, chiefly to minimise mass while maximising structural strength, widely used in aerospace

◦ Additive manufacturing (3D printing) — building objects layer by layer

◦ Blockchain — a distributed, tamper-evident digital ledger

◦ Edge computing — processing data close to its source rather than in a distant cloud

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Encrypting data on a distributed ledger describes blockchain, not a digital twin.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Duplicating servers at a remote site is disaster-recovery mirroring in information technology.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Replacing physical prototypes with printed models describes rapid prototyping through 3D printing.

question: Which cell organelle is known as the 'protein factory' of the cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ribosome.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ribosomes are called the "protein factories" of the cell because they are the site of protein synthesis (translation), where amino acids are assembled into polypeptide chains according to the message carried by mRNA. (राइबोसोम — प्रोटीन की फैक्ट्री)

 

• Ribosomes are non-membrane-bound organelles made of RNA and protein. They are found free in the cytoplasm and attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum, and are also present inside mitochondria and chloroplasts. They were discovered by George Palade.

 

• Ribosomes of prokaryotic cells are of the 70S type, while those of the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells are 80S.

 

• Common nicknames of other organelles:

◦ Mitochondrion — "powerhouse of the cell"

◦ Lysosome — "suicide bag of the cell", the site of intracellular digestion

◦ Golgi apparatus — "post office" or "traffic police" of the cell, which packages and dispatches materials

◦ Nucleus — "control room" or "brain" of the cell

◦ Endoplasmic reticulum — the cell's transport and synthesis network

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The cell was discovered by Robert Hooke in 1665, who observed cork under a microscope; Anton van Leeuwenhoek first saw living cells; and the cell theory was proposed by Schleiden and Schwann and completed by Rudolf Virchow ("omnis cellula e cellula").

 

• Plant cells differ from animal cells in having a cell wall (of cellulose), plastids and a large central vacuole; centrioles are typically absent.

 

NOTE

 

• The Golgi apparatus (Option 1): Modifies, packages and dispatches proteins and lipids; discovered by Camillo Golgi.

 

• The lysosome (Option 2): Contains hydrolytic enzymes and carries out intracellular digestion and the removal of worn-out organelles.

 

• The centrosome (Option 3): Contains the centrioles and organises the spindle fibres during cell division.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding the Finance Commission of India are correct?

1) It is constituted by the President under Article 280 every fifth year, or earlier if he considers it necessary.

2) It recommends the distribution of the net proceeds of shareable taxes between the Union and the States.

3) Its recommendations are binding on the Government of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. Article 280 requires the President to constitute a Finance Commission at the expiration of every fifth year, or at such earlier time as he considers necessary. It consists of a chairman and four other members. (वित्त आयोग — अनुच्छेद 280)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. The Commission recommends the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes to be shared between the Union and the States, and the allocation of the respective shares among the States; the principles governing grants-in-aid to the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India; and measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of panchayats and municipalities.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are advisory only and are not binding on the Government of India. It is left to the Union Government to implement them; by convention, however, the recommendations on tax devolution have generally been accepted.

 

• The First Finance Commission was set up in 1951 under K.C. Neogy. The 15th Finance Commission, chaired by N.K. Singh, recommended a 41 per cent share for the States in the divisible pool of central taxes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 270 deals with the distribution of taxes levied and collected by the Union and shared with the States. After the 101st Constitutional Amendment (2016), which introduced the Goods and Services Tax, Article 270 also covers the distribution of the Union's share of GST (CGST and IGST). The GST Compensation Cess, however, is not shared under Article 270.

 

• The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A, chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

 

• The Finance Commission is often described as the balancing wheel of fiscal federalism in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1 and 4 are incorrect because they include Statement 3, and the Commission's recommendations are recommendatory, not binding.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect because it leaves out Statement 2, which correctly describes the Commission's principal function.

question: If the distance between two bodies is doubled while their masses remain unchanged, the gravitational force of attraction between them becomes:
solution_text:
The correct answer is One-fourth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation, the force of attraction between two bodies is F = G m₁m₂ / r², that is, it is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres. (गुरुत्वाकर्षण का सार्वत्रिक नियम)

 

• Since F ∝ 1/r², if the distance is doubled (r → 2r), the force becomes F' = G m₁m₂ / (2r)² = G m₁m₂ / 4r² = F/4. The force therefore falls to one-fourth of its original value.

 

• The universal gravitational constant G is 6.674 x 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². It is a scalar and its value is the same everywhere in the universe, unlike g, the acceleration due to gravity, which varies with location.

 

• The value of g at the Earth's surface is about 9.8 m/s², and g = GM/R². So if the Earth's radius were reduced while its mass stayed the same, g would increase; a 1 per cent reduction in radius raises g by roughly 2 per cent, because g varies as 1/R².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The value of g is maximum at the poles and minimum at the equator, because the Earth is slightly flattened at the poles. It decreases with altitude and also decreases with depth, becoming zero at the centre of the Earth.

 

• The value of g on the Moon is about 1/6 of that on the Earth. Mass is a constant scalar measured in kilograms, whereas weight (W = mg) is a force measured in newtons and changes with location.

 

NOTE

 

• Double (Option 1) and Four times (Option 3) are incorrect: increasing the separation reduces the force, it does not increase it.

 

• Half (Option 2) is incorrect: it would be the answer only if the force varied as 1/r, whereas gravitation follows an inverse-square law.

question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), within what maximum period must a person who has been arrested be produced before the nearest magistrate, excluding the time necessary for the journey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 24 hours.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, a person who has been arrested must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of the arrest, excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court. (गिरफ़्तारी के 24 घंटे के भीतर मजिस्ट्रेट के समक्ष प्रस्तुति)

 

• This is not merely a statutory requirement but also a Fundamental Right under Article 22(2) of the Constitution, which guarantees that no arrested person shall be detained in custody beyond twenty-four hours without the authority of a magistrate.

 

• The safeguards of Article 22(1) and 22(2) — the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest, to consult a legal practitioner of one's choice, and to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours — are not available to enemy aliens or to persons detained under a law of preventive detention.

 

• The BNSS also caps police custody at 15 days, but allows this period to be sought in parts during the first 40 or 60 days of the total period of judicial remand, depending on the gravity of the offence — a change from the earlier CrPC position.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three new criminal laws, in force from 1 July 2024, are the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replacing the IPC 1860, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) replacing the CrPC 1973, and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) replacing the Indian Evidence Act 1872.

 

• The maximum period of default bail entitlement arises if the investigation is not completed within 60 days (offences punishable with less than 10 years) or 90 days (offences punishable with death, life imprisonment or 10 years or more).

 

• In D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1997), the Supreme Court laid down detailed guidelines on arrest and detention to prevent custodial abuse.

 

NOTE

 

• 12 hours (Option 1), 48 hours (Option 3) and 72 hours (Option 4) are incorrect. The constitutional and statutory limit is 24 hours, and any detention beyond it without a magistrate's authorisation is illegal.

question: Under the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) scheme, an enrolled unorganised worker is assured a minimum monthly pension of how much after attaining the age of 60 years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rs. 3,000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM), launched in February 2019 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, assures a minimum monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 to enrolled unorganised workers after they attain the age of 60 years. (प्रधानमंत्री श्रम योगी मानधन — 3,000 रुपये मासिक पेंशन)

 

• It is a voluntary and contributory scheme on a 50:50 matching basis — whatever monthly contribution the worker makes, an equal amount is contributed by the Central Government.

 

• Eligibility: unorganised workers such as street vendors, rickshaw pullers, domestic workers, agricultural labourers and construction workers, aged 18 to 40 years, with a monthly income of Rs. 15,000 or less, who are not covered by EPFO, ESIC or NPS and are not income-tax payers.

 

• On the death of the subscriber after pension has commenced, the spouse receives 50 per cent of the pension as a family pension.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Two sister schemes on the same design also assure Rs. 3,000 a month at the age of 60, for the entry age group of 18 to 40 years:

◦ Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY), 2019 — for small and marginal farmers holding up to 2 hectares

◦ National Pension Scheme for Traders and Self-Employed Persons (NPS-Traders), 2019 — for retail traders and shopkeepers with turnover up to Rs. 1.5 crore

 

• Other social security schemes: the Atal Pension Yojana (2015), which gives a guaranteed pension of Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000 a month, and the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana and Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, both launched in 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• Rs. 1,000 (Option 1): The minimum guaranteed monthly pension under the Atal Pension Yojana, and also the minimum pension under the EPS-95.

 

• Rs. 5,000 (Option 4): The maximum monthly pension available under the Atal Pension Yojana, not the PM-SYM entitlement.

 

• Rs. 2,000 (Option 2) is incorrect; it corresponds to no benefit level under PM-SYM.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:

Assertion (A): The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan seeks to reduce the logistics cost of the Indian economy.

Reason (R): It provides a GIS-based digital platform that brings several infrastructure ministries onto a common map for integrated planning of projects.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, launched on 13 October 2021, is a Rs. 100 lakh crore initiative for multi-modal connectivity, whose central aim is to cut India's logistics cost, which has been estimated at a high share of GDP compared with developed economies. (पीएम गति शक्ति राष्ट्रीय मास्टर प्लान)

 

• Reason (R) is true. It is a GIS-based digital platform, developed with the help of BISAG-N, that brings 16 ministries — including Railways, Roads, Ports, Aviation, Power and Telecom — onto a single unified map with hundreds of data layers.

 

• R correctly explains A. Logistics costs in India were high largely because ministries planned and executed infrastructure in silos, causing duplication, delays and missing last-mile links. By putting all agencies on one platform for integrated, synchronised planning, Gati Shakti removes precisely those inefficiencies — so the digital platform is the very mechanism by which the cost reduction is achieved.

 

• Gati Shakti rests on six pillars: comprehensiveness, prioritisation, optimisation, synchronisation, analytical capability and dynamism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Logistics Policy, launched in September 2022, complements Gati Shakti and aims to bring logistics costs down and to place India among the top rankers in the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index.

 

• The UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) scheme, launched in 2016 under the National Civil Aviation Policy, improves regional air connectivity by capping fares and providing Viability Gap Funding to airlines operating on unserved and underserved routes.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: R is not an unrelated fact; the integrated digital platform is the direct means of lowering logistics costs.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.

question: The Global Hunger Index, which ranks countries on the basis of undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality, is published jointly by which two organisations?
option_2: The FAO and the World Food Programme
option_3: The World Bank and the IMF
solution_text:
The correct answer is Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Global Hunger Index (GHI) is published jointly by Concern Worldwide, an Irish humanitarian organisation, and Welthungerhilfe, a German aid agency. (ग्लोबल हंगर इंडेक्स)

 

• The index is calculated from four indicators:

◦ Undernourishment — the share of the population with insufficient calorie intake

◦ Child stunting — the share of children under five who have low height for their age

◦ Child wasting — the share of children under five who have low weight for their height

◦ Child mortality — the death rate of children under the age of five

 

• Scores are given on a 100-point scale, where 0 is the best (no hunger) and 100 the worst, and countries are graded as low, moderate, serious, alarming or extremely alarming.

 

• The Government of India has on several occasions questioned the methodology of the GHI, pointing out that three of the four indicators relate only to children and that the undernourishment estimate rests on a small opinion poll sample.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important global indices and their publishers:

◦ Human Development Index — UNDP

◦ Global Innovation Index — WIPO

◦ World Happiness Report — UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network

◦ Ease of Doing Business (discontinued) and the Logistics Performance Index — World Bank

◦ Global Competitiveness Report and the Global Gender Gap Report — World Economic Forum

◦ Corruption Perceptions Index — Transparency International

◦ Global Cities Index — Oxford Economics

 

NOTE

 

• The FAO and the WFP (Option 2): Along with IFAD, UNICEF and WHO, they publish the annual State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) report, which is a different publication.

 

• The World Bank and the IMF (Option 3): Publish the World Development Report and the World Economic Outlook respectively.

 

• UNDP and UNICEF (Option 4): UNDP publishes the Human Development Report; UNICEF publishes the State of the World's Children.

question: Which of the following is an example of a basic or key industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron and steel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On the basis of their role, industries are divided into basic (key) industries and consumer industries. (आधारभूत उद्योग एवं उपभोक्ता उद्योग)

 

• Basic or key industries are those whose products are used as raw materials by other industries. Examples are iron and steel, copper smelting and aluminium smelting. Iron and steel is the classic example, since its output feeds engineering, construction, automobile, shipbuilding and machine-tool industries.

 

• Consumer industries produce goods for direct use by consumers, such as sugar, paper, toothpaste, sewing machines, fans and toiletries.

 

• Industries are also classified on other bases:

◦ Raw materials — agro-based (cotton, sugar, tea), mineral-based (iron and steel, cement), marine-based, forest-based

◦ Bulk and weight — heavy industries (iron and steel) and light industries, which use light raw materials to produce consumer goods (electronics, watches)

◦ Ownership — public sector, private sector, joint sector and cooperative sector

◦ Size — small scale and large scale

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The iron and steel industry requires four principal raw materials — iron ore, coking coal, limestone and dolomite — in roughly the ratio 4:2:1, so plants are located near the sources of these bulky materials.

 

• India's major steel plants are at Bhilai (Chhattisgarh), Rourkela (Odisha), Durgapur (West Bengal), Bokaro (Jharkhand) and Burnpur; the oldest is TISCO at Jamshedpur, established in 1907 by Jamsetji Tata. India is among the largest crude steel producers in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Sugar (Option 1) and Paper (Option 2): Both are agro-based consumer industries; their products go directly to consumers.

 

• Toothpaste (Option 3): A typical consumer industry product, made largely from light raw materials.

question:
Fill in the blank:

The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India contains ______.
option_1: The forms of oaths and affirmations
option_2: The list of recognised official languages
option_3: The provisions relating to disqualification on the ground of defection
option_4: The allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha
solution_text:
The correct answer is The list of recognised official languages.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution lists the languages recognised by the Constitution. It originally contained 14 languages and now contains 22. (आठवीं अनुसूची — 22 भाषाएँ)

 

• Languages added later were Sindhi by the 21st Amendment (1967); Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali by the 71st Amendment (1992); and Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali by the 92nd Amendment (2003).

 

• The important Schedules of the Constitution:

◦ First Schedule — the States and Union Territories

◦ Second Schedule — emoluments of the President, Governors, judges and other office-holders

◦ Third Schedule — forms of oaths and affirmations

◦ Fourth Schedule — allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha

◦ Fifth and Sixth Schedules — administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas

◦ Seventh Schedule — the three legislative lists (Union, State and Concurrent)

◦ Ninth Schedule — laws protected from judicial review, added by the 1st Amendment (1951)

◦ Tenth Schedule — the anti-defection law, added by the 52nd Amendment (1985)

◦ Eleventh Schedule — panchayats, 29 subjects, 73rd Amendment (1992)

◦ Twelfth Schedule — municipalities, 18 subjects, 74th Amendment (1992)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Constitution originally had 8 Schedules; there are now 12.

 

• Hindi in the Devanagari script is the official language of the Union under Article 343, and English continues as an associate official language. Being in the Eighth Schedule does not by itself make a language an official language of the Union.

 

• As of now, the languages that have been given classical language status include Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali.

 

NOTE

 

• The forms of oaths and affirmations (Option 1) are in the Third Schedule.

 

• The anti-defection provisions (Option 3) are in the Tenth Schedule.

 

• The allocation of Rajya Sabha seats (Option 4) is in the Fourth Schedule.

question: A state government promotes rooftop solar installations and replaces its diesel bus fleet with electric buses in order to cut greenhouse gas emissions. This action falls primarily under which category of climate change response?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Climate Change Mitigation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Climate change mitigation means action taken to reduce or prevent the emission of greenhouse gases, or to enhance the sinks that absorb them — in short, tackling the causes of climate change. (जलवायु परिवर्तन शमन — कारणों का समाधान)

 

• Promoting rooftop solar power and switching from diesel to electric buses both reduce the burning of fossil fuels and therefore cut carbon dioxide emissions at source. These are textbook mitigation measures.

 

• Climate change adaptation, by contrast, means adjusting to the effects of climate change that are already occurring or expected — for example, building sea walls, elevating buildings, developing drought-resistant crop varieties, constructing cyclone shelters and improving early-warning systems.

 

• The simplest way to distinguish them: mitigation addresses the cause (emissions), while adaptation addresses the consequence (impacts).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's mitigation commitments under its updated Nationally Determined Contributions include reducing the emissions intensity of GDP by 45 per cent from 2005 levels by 2030, achieving about 50 per cent of installed electric power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030, and reaching net zero by 2070.

 

• The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), 2008, runs eight national missions, including the National Solar Mission, the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency and the National Water Mission.

 

• The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), established in 1988 by the WMO and UNEP, assesses the science of climate change and shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007.

 

NOTE

 

• Climate Change Adaptation (Option 1): Would cover sea walls, elevated buildings or drought-resistant crops — measures that cope with impacts rather than cut emissions.

 

• Carbon Sequestration (Option 3): The capture and long-term storage of carbon dioxide, in forests, soil or underground reservoirs. It is one specific tool within mitigation, but it does not describe solar power or electric buses.

 

• Geoengineering (Option 4): Large-scale deliberate intervention in the Earth's climate system, such as solar radiation management by injecting aerosols into the stratosphere.

question: The minimum velocity with which a body must be projected so that it escapes permanently from the gravitational field of the Earth is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Escape velocity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Escape velocity is the minimum velocity required for a body to overcome the Earth's gravitational pull and escape from it permanently, never to return. (पलायन वेग)

 

• Its value for the Earth is about 11.2 km/s, that is roughly 40,320 km/h. It is given by v = √(2GM/R), and equivalently v = √(2gR).

 

• Escape velocity does not depend on the mass of the escaping body or on the direction of projection; it depends only on the mass and radius of the planet. It is √2 times the orbital velocity of a satellite close to the Earth's surface.

 

• Orbital velocity is the velocity needed to keep a satellite in a stable orbit, given by v = √(GM/r). For a satellite orbiting close to the Earth it is about 7.9 km/s. It is because a satellite already possesses the required orbital velocity that it stays in orbit without continuous propulsion — gravity supplies exactly the centripetal force needed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Escape velocity on the Moon is only about 2.4 km/s, which is why the Moon has been unable to retain an atmosphere. On Jupiter it is about 59.5 km/s.

 

• A geostationary satellite orbits at a height of about 36,000 km above the equator with a period of 24 hours, so that it appears stationary from the Earth. INSAT and GSAT are Indian geostationary satellite series, while IRS satellites are placed in polar sun-synchronous orbits.

 

NOTE

 

• Orbital velocity (Option 1): The velocity required to stay in orbit, about 7.9 km/s near the Earth's surface, not to escape.

 

• Terminal velocity (Option 2): The constant maximum velocity attained by a body falling through a fluid when the drag force balances the weight.

 

• Critical velocity (Option 3): The velocity of flow at which fluid motion changes from streamline (laminar) to turbulent.
